name: Reply to P4 regrade request (late days)

content.text: cs3604 regrade dispute. student says their P4 shouldn't have a late penalty because they used "grace days". syllabus: 3 late days total for the semester, P4 submitted 2 days late, but they already used 2 days on P2. so 1 day free, 1 day penalized (10%). they're upset. draft a reply, firm but nice, short. final grades due 12/15

Hi [Name],

Thanks for flagging this. I checked your late-day usage for the semester:

- P2: submitted 2 days late (2 late days used)
- P4: submitted 2 days late

The syllabus allows 3 late days total, so 1 of your P4 days was covered and the second was penalized at the standard 10%. That's why your P4 score shows the deduction.

I know that's frustrating at the end of the semester. If you think the P2 count is wrong (for example, if you had an approved extension), send me the details and I'll look again before final grades are submitted on Dec 15.

Best,
David
they did have an extension on P2 actually, i just checked canvas comments, prof approved 1 day for a doctors note

Then the count changes: P2 used only 1 late day, so they had 2 left for P4 and no penalty applies. Revised reply:

Hi [Name],

Thanks for flagging this, and you're right. Your P2 had an approved 1-day extension, so it only used 1 late day. That leaves 2 for P4, which covers both days. I've removed the 10% deduction; your P4 score should update in Canvas by tomorrow.

Sorry for the confusion.

Best,
David

Also worth checking whether the rubric sheet's late-day column has other approved extensions that weren't applied; if this one was missed, others might be.
good point ill check the sheet
If the sheet has a column for extensions, a quick filter on "extension noted but late days not adjusted" will catch them. Better to find them before 12/15 than in January.
